y-m-55-04.title: If two values equal for two x values, na identity?
y-m-55-04.goal: Judge whether fact say two expressions equal for some values give enough evidence for 'na identity'; revise judgment when new value show up, and tell equation apart from identity.
y-m-55-04.material: Sora dey put x values one by one and compare expressions x²+x and 2x ('x squared plus x', and '2 times x') to know whether dem be 'identity in x' (case where both expressions always equal no matter which real x value you put inside).

y-m-55-04.thinking.2: Separate equation (only hold for some x) from identity (hold for every x)

y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.info: If you put x=0, x²+x=0 and 2x=0, so both values equal.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: Looking only at this result, how you go judge 'both expressions be identity in x'?

y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.o.a: We fit conclude say na identity.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: We fit conclude say na identity.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This thinking take equality at one value as evidence of equality at every value.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Dem equal at only one value, so e too early to decide.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This judgment recognize say only one piece of evidence dey.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: We fit conclude say e no be identity.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Same value come out, so no reason dey to conclude right away say e no be.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.o.d: x=0 special value, so make we put other values in before deciding.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: This judgment wan test other values, no be only value like 0 wey look special.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.info: If you put x=1, x²+x=2 and 2x=2, so both values equal again.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: Both values equal for two x values. Wetin you judge now?

y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This thinking take same result wey show two times as evidence of equality for every x.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: The chance don increase, but we no fit conclude yet.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This judgment raise confidence as evidence increase but still delay conclusion.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Now we conclude say e no be identity.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Only equal values show up, so no reason dey to conclude the opposite.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Simplify x²+x−2x and find the x values wey make am 0.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This judgment wan use expression itself to check answer instead of putting in more values.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.info: If you put x=2, x²+x=6 and 2x=4, so values different.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: With this new result, wetin happen to your judgment?
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.after: Values different at x=2, so e no be identity. Checking calculation one time reasonable too, but result still 6 and 4.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Na identity because both values match for two x values.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This thinking treat new opposite evidence as weaker than earlier evidence.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: E no be identity, because at least one x give different values.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This judgment use one counterexample to break general claim.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: This careful judgment check possibility say counterexample come from calculation mistake.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.o.d: x=2 special value, so we ignore this result.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: This thinking try throw away evidence wey no agree with your own judgment.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.3.info: Since x²+x−2x=x²−x=x(x−1), both expressions equal only when x=0 or x=1.

y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.3.after: The x=0 and 1 values wey equal before na exactly solutions to this equation. Even for same expressions, if dem 'hold only at some x', na equation; if dem 'hold for every x', na identity.

y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.3.r.b: This thinking forget say both values equal at x=1 too.
y-m-55-04.s.s1.st.3.r.c: This thinking no fit tell identity from equation.

y-m-55-04.s.s1.reflect: Equality at x=0 and x=1 support idea say 'maybe na identity', but e no be proof; one x with different value, x=2, change the judgment. If same expressions equal 'only for some x', that na equation solution; if dem equal 'for every x', that na identity.

y-m-55-04.s.s2.modelNote.1: Answer wey use 'special values' instead of word 'solutions' still correct.

y-m-55-06.title: Can approximation alone tell which number bigger?
y-m-55-06.goal: Learn approximation cutoffs sometimes no decide size; tell when error range fit give conclusion and when exact comparison needed.
y-m-55-06.material: A=√2+√3 (root 2 plus root 3), B=√10 (root 10). We wan know which bigger. No calculator; instead each step give more digits of 'number value after decimal digits cut off'. We no know how much cut off.
y-m-55-06.thinking.1: Change judgment/confidence as more information arrive
y-m-55-06.prereq.0: Square roots and approximation like √2≈1.4 (middle school)
y-m-55-06.prereq.1: Squaring two positive numbers no change size order
y-m-55-06.s.s1.prompt: For each new info, choose judgment about which A,B bigger. You fit change judgment next step.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.hint.0: At each step, write lower and upper limits for ranges A and B dey inside.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.hint.1: After compare whether ranges overlap, choose judgment.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.info: Values cut after first decimal: √2 at least 1.4 and below 1.5; √3 at least 1.7 and below 1.8; √10 at least 3.1 and below 3.2.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.after: A at least 3.1 and below 3.3; B at least 3.1 and below 3.2, so ranges overlap. No decision yet.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You see only A range extend above 3.3, but check part overlapping B range. A upper range 3.3, lower range 3.1.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You trust feeling √10 for B bigger. First check ranges overlap?
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You think equal because cut-off values equal. Even same cutoff place, discarded parts different.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.o.d: We no fit know from this info alone
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.0.r.d: This judgment check whether two number ranges overlap.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.info: Two-decimal values for √2 and √3 now known: √2=1.41..., √3=1.73...; √10 still only to one decimal (≥3.1,<3.2). So A range now ≥3.14 and <3.16.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.after: A range ≥3.14,<3.16; B ≥3.1,<3.2, so overlap. Even if only A become exact, wide B range no allow decision. B need more accurate digits too.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.o.a: A at least 3.14 and below 3.16; B at least 3.1 and below 3.2; ranges overlap, so no decision yet
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This judgment compare range endpoints and check overlap.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.o.b: A range ≥3.14, and B dey 3.1 something, so A bigger
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.r.b: B range still wide: ≥3.1 and <3.2. Compare A biggest value with B smallest.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Compare range ends, no follow feeling. Check current overlap.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Check if decision fit happen when B too known to two decimals
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This judgment know one side getting exact still allow ranges overlap; decide what next info needed.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.after: A<3.16≤B, so B bigger. Even using approximations alone, non-overlapping error ranges let us conclude.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.o.a: A and B ranges overlap, so still unknown
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You see both near 3.16 and think overlap. Check difference between 'less than' and 'at least'.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.o.b: A<3.16 and B≥3.16, so B bigger
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This judgment compare range ends to decide which bigger.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Approximation got error, so conclusion never possible
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Even with error, non-overlapping ranges allow conclusion.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You no compare A upper end with B lower end.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.info: Can compare exactly without approximation too. A²=(√2+√3)²=5+2√6, B²=10. Compare 5+2√6 and 10 by comparing 2√6 and 5; 2√6=√24, 5=√25.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.ask: How should we judge this method?
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.after: √24<√25, so A²<B²; both positive, therefore A<B. Same result as approximation, no need worry about error.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.o.a: Squaring reverse order, so B smaller
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.r.a: You wrongly apply reversal for negative numbers to positive numbers.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.o.b: Radicals remain, no compare without approximation
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.r.b: We fit compare √24 and √25 by numbers inside radical too.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.o.c: Both positive, squaring keep order, exact comparison possible
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.r.c: This checks condition say squaring positive numbers preserve order.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.o.d: Squaring change values, so no use for comparison
y-m-55-06.s.s1.st.3.r.d: Values change, but if order same, e still useful comparison.
y-m-55-06.s.s1.reflect: At first estimate alone no decide; when only one side get more digits ranges overlap. With more digits on both, ranges stop overlap and conclusion possible. Judgment change no be because numbers 'look reasonable' but because range endpoints compared. Estimate and exact method same conclusion.
